T-cell receptor-related genes are highly conserved in the vertebrate lineage and that these genes appear to have evolved before the emergence of the jawed vertebrates.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a strategy that allows the isolation of TCR and Ig genes from a wide variety of vertebrate species.
the TCR and Ig gene superfamily are present in all vertebrate species examined and are highly similar in structure and organization to their mammalian counterparts.
